original_card.question: Can one uncovered interface implication be formalized with exact caller and certificate bindings?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one missing statement with quantified hypotheses, actual caller and existing coverage. A compact-switch lemma is a candidate only after its mathematical contract is reviewed. Establish a bounded proof plan before a separately budgeted proof-assistant build; do not rerun large Lean jobs as orientation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

existing_checks.remaining: Exact theorem-to-caller binding and genuinely uncovered interface lemmas.
Uniform algorithmic implications, not another endpoint digit.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: compact-switch formalization proposed as future validation.
existing_checks.remaining: Audit the statement and assumptions before a formal proof campaign.

actual_scope: Guidance package for the P104 lower-bound programme on top of #7852: precise open targets (NET-D56 drop form, R side, caller mid-k window, loose decoder rows, general decoder wall), exact stdlib-checkable certificates (Q = 0 full-LP duals for k = 71..73 and Q >= 1 thin-column duals for k = 13, 76..120), exact witnesses (15 legal tight Q = 0 caller words k = 3..13, direct-sum tightness, TIGHT55 symmetry gap, R = 2 < mass 3 run, DECOMP word), all lane notes and our own lane scripts as data, and eleven same-day Lean sources not rebuilt here. No kappa claim. The k = 72/73 bounds are conditional LP bounds whose extra rows are paper-[P].
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one formal interface lemma; this package is a guidance and data package (open targets, certificates, witnesses, notes), so the scope is changed.
bottleneck_link: Side result (guidance and data). States the open cores of the lower-bound programme exactly and supplies exactly checkable witnesses and certificates so contributors can attack them without re-deriving the lane results.
stop_rule: Ship only if verify.py passes (pins, token scan, scrub scan, certificate verifiers, witness checks) and the research-package validator passes; otherwise report the failing check.
evidence: verify.py (stdlib): sha256 pins both directions; Lean token bans in lean_extra; scrub scan; certs/verify_q0.py and verify_q1.py (exact weak duality, partition DP); data/q0_callers/check_all.py; data/direct_sum, data/tight55_gap checks; code/ctcover/ctsplit.py and code/decomp/dc1.py outputs.
author: DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code
ai_assistance: Prepared with Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code under DreamingOfClouds' direction. Certificates and witnesses are checked by stdlib scripts; the notes are lane write-ups not individually re-audited (see CORRECTIONS.md). No independent human acceptance is claimed.

open_questions.question: Is there a network-coding gain on Q96 (level slices of rank >= 9)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the single question behind NET-D56 (D side) and ChainWall56@Q96 (R side) and gates every conditional rung statement.
open_questions.first_step: Prove JUNK-PAYS-inv or find a legal -I@Q96 network with D <= 55.
open_questions.blocked_by: No proof or counterexample is known; level-cut proofs must use D <= 55.
